### Basis of preparation

All amounts are **USD as of June 30, 2025**. The primary case applies management’s definition strictly: **current annualized contracted recurring revenue from live customers**. It excludes future ramps, implementation fees, unsigned renewals, services not yet live, and usage revenue without a contractual minimum. Termination and renewal risks are disclosed separately, not deducted from current ARR.

### 1. Customer reconciliation

**Adjustment = adjusted ARR − management ARR.**

| Customer | Management ARR | Adjusted ARR | Adjustment ($) | Issue category | Basis / formula |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| C1 — Atlas Freight | $420,000 | $360,000 | −$60,000 | Ramp | June 2025 falls in Year 2: **$360,000**. Adjustment = $360,000 − $420,000. Year 3 pricing is not current ARR. |
| C2 — Birchway Foods | $310,000 | $260,000 | −$50,000 | One-time fee | $310,000 − $50,000 implementation fee = **$260,000** recurring subscription. |
| C3 — Cobalt Mining | $275,000 | $0 | −$275,000 | Expired / presumed churned | Contract expired; renewal unsigned and usage ceased. No supported current contracted ARR: **$0**. |
| C4 — Delmar Transit | $240,000 | $240,000 | $0 | Termination risk | Current annual subscription = **$240,000**; convenience termination affects durability, not current ARR. |
| C5 — Evergreen Utilities | $198,000 | $198,000 | $0 | Renewal risk | Current annual subscription = **$198,000**; expires June 30, 2026. |
| C6 — Fairhaven Logistics | $180,000 | $144,000 | −$36,000 | Discount | $15,000 × (1 − 20%) × 12 = **$144,000**, corroborated by June invoice: $12,000 × 12. |
| C7 — Granite Builders | $150,000 | $150,000 | $0 | None | Current annual subscription = **$150,000**. |
| C8 — Halcyon Retail | $132,000 | $0 | −$132,000 | Not live | September 1 service start; not onboarded. Live ARR = **$0**; separately disclose $132,000 signed backlog. |
| C9 — Ironwood Ag | $120,000 | $87,600 | −$32,400 | FX | CAD 120,000 × 0.73 USD/CAD = **$87,600**. |
| C10 — Juniper Couriers | $75,000 | $0 | −$75,000 | Usage-based | Contractual minimum = **$0**; primary case excludes uncommitted consumption. Alternatives below. |
| **Total** | **$2,100,000** | **$1,439,600** | **−$660,400** | | **Sum of customer rows.** |

#### Judgment calls and alternatives

| Item | Alternative treatment and formula | Impact versus primary case |
|---|---|---|
| C6 | Use post-discount contracted run-rate: $15,000 × 12 = **$180,000**. This anticipates January 2026 pricing rather than measuring June pricing. | ARR **+$36,000**, to **$1,475,600**; value at 6.0× **+$216,000**. |
| C10 — trailing usage | If recurring consumption is accepted as ARR: [($4,750 + $5,500 + $6,250) ÷ 3] × 12 = **$66,000**. Preferable to extrapolating one month, but not contractually committed. | ARR **+$66,000**, to **$1,505,600**; value **+$396,000**. |
| C10 — June run-rate | June invoice × 12 = $6,250 × 12 = **$75,000**, matching management. More sensitive to recent usage growth. | ARR **+$75,000**, to **$1,514,600**; value **+$450,000**. |

Each alternative is shown independently; the two C10 alternatives are mutually exclusive.

### 2. ARR bridge

| Bridge item | Change / separate amount | Running live ARR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Management ARR | $2,100,000 | $2,100,000 |
| Ramp — C1 | −$60,000 | $2,040,000 |
| One-time fee — C2 | −$50,000 | $1,990,000 |
| Expired / presumed churned — C3 | −$275,000 | $1,715,000 |
| Current discount — C6 | −$36,000 | $1,679,000 |
| Not live — C8 | −$132,000 | $1,547,000 |
| FX — C9 | −$32,400 | $1,514,600 |
| Uncommitted usage — C10 | −$75,000 | **$1,439,600** |
| **Adjusted live ARR** | **$2,100,000 − $660,400** | **$1,439,600** |
| **Separate: contracted-but-not-live ARR — C8** | **$132,000 annual subscription** | **Excluded above** |

Adjusted live ARR plus signed, not-live ARR would be **$1,439,600 + $132,000 = $1,571,600**, but that is not June 30 live ARR.

### 3. Risk-weighted view: next 12 months

No loss probabilities are provided, so an expected-value haircut would be unsupported. The table identifies **gross ARR exposure**, not predicted losses.

| Customer / exposure | Reason | ARR at stake |
|---|---|---:|
| C4 — Delmar Transit | Ninety-day convenience termination notice may be given after September 30, 2025, permitting termination around year-end 2025 onward despite the stated 2027 expiry. | $240,000 |
| C5 — Evergreen Utilities | Contract expires June 30, 2026, at the end of the forward 12-month window; renewal exposure, not evidence of churn. | $198,000 |
| **Primary-case exposure** | $240,000 + $198,000 = **$438,000**; $438,000 ÷ $1,439,600 = **30.43%** of adjusted ARR. | **$438,000** |
| C10 — conditional exposure only | If included under a usage-based alternative, all annualized usage is exposed to consumption changes, with no minimum floor. Not included in the total above. | $66,000 or $75,000 |

If both C4 and C5 were lost completely, with no offsets, ARR would be **$1,439,600 − $438,000 = $1,001,600**. C6’s discount expiry is potential upside, not an identified contractual revenue loss.

### 4. Customer concentration

| Rank | Customer | Adjusted ARR | Share of adjusted ARR |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | Atlas Freight | $360,000 | $360,000 ÷ $1,439,600 = **25.01%** |
| 2 | Birchway Foods | $260,000 | $260,000 ÷ $1,439,600 = **18.06%** |
| 3 | Delmar Transit | $240,000 | $240,000 ÷ $1,439,600 = **16.67%** |
| **Top 3** | | **$860,000** | $860,000 ÷ $1,439,600 = **59.74%** |

### 5. Investment committee summary

| Key takeaways |
|---|
| • **Diligence-adjusted live ARR is $1,439,600**, down $660,400, or **31.45%** ($660,400 ÷ $2,100,000), from management. |
| • At **6.0× ARR**, indicated purchase price falls from **$12,600,000** to **$8,637,600**: a **$3,962,400 reduction**, holding the multiple and other price adjustments constant. |
| • **$132,000 of signed, not-live ARR** should remain separate until service commencement; it is not June live ARR. |
| • **$438,000 of current ARR is exposed to termination or renewal within 12 months**; obtain Delmar retention evidence and Evergreen renewal visibility. |
| • The top three customers represent **59.74%** of adjusted ARR, including termination-exposed Delmar. |
| • Agree the ARR definition before pricing: C6 normalization adds **$36,000**, while accepting C10 usage adds **$66,000–$75,000**; these are alternatives, not primary-case ARR. |
